note.note:
Action Plan:
1) Right knee pain with clicking during exercise:
   - Activity modification: Ease up on running; do not run through pain. Continue regular ice therapy.
   - Medication: A stronger anti-inflammatory was prescribed to be taken regularly with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen or other NSAIDs. Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy. (Name/dose/route/frequency not documented.)
   - Referral: Physiotherapy referral for comprehensive knee assessment and management.
   - Imaging: Consider imaging after physiotherapy assessment if indicated (e.g., to assess cartilage/meniscus).
   - Safety-net: Seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.
   - If physiotherapy wait is long, arrange clinic assessment.
2) Transient tingling in right toes after a run:
   - No current symptoms. Monitor for recurrence; no immediate tests or treatment planned per this consult.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Knee pain and clicking with exercise; concern about overuse; occasional toe tingling.
- History of presenting illness:
  - Onset/duration: ~2 weeks.
  - Laterality/location: Right knee; pain felt centrally, possibly more on the right/lateral side.
  - Course/triggers: Begins ~20 minutes into runs (~2.5–3 miles); worsened enough to stop last run. Clicking noted during gym ab exercises involving repeated knee flexion/extension. No pain at rest.
  - Swelling: Mild swelling after first run, resolved with ice; currently no swelling.
  - Function: Full ability to fully flex/extend; no locking; no giving way; no pain with stairs or normal walking.
  - Neurovascular: One episode of tingling in right toes after a run; no persistent numbness; no color/temperature change; no calf pain.
- Past medical/surgical history:
  - Farsighted; prior LASIK.
  - Prior severe UTI episode (evaluated for possible kidney stones).
  - Sports: Plays ice hockey; fall months ago causing a bruise; no ongoing joint problems reported.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed.
  - Aleve as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Vitamin D (dose/frequency not documented).
  - Melatonin (dose/frequency not documented).
  - Alprazolam (Xanax) occasionally for sleep (dose/frequency not documented).
  - Occasional cannabis use (smokes a joint).
- Social history:
  - Training for a marathon (started longer runs ~1 month ago; currently 4–8 mile runs).
  - Gym a few times per week.
  - Lives in London.
  - Notes sock indentations with prolonged standing (dependent swelling).
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals recorded.
- Patient-reported knee status:
  - Right knee: currently no swelling; full active range of motion; no locking or instability; pain triggered by sustained running; clicking with repetitive flexion/extension during gym exercises.
  - No pain with stairs or walking.
- Neurovascular: Single post-run episode of right toe tingling; currently resolved; no discoloration or temperature change; no calf pain.
- Investigations: None performed.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Right knee pain with clicking during exercise:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Iliotibial band friction syndrome (ITBFS) – High (DDx).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) – Medium (DDx). Supports: crepitus/clicking with flexion/extension, running-related; Opposes: no pain on stairs or prolonged sitting; pain not clearly anterior.
     - Meniscal pathology (degenerative/minor tear) – Low-Medium (DDx). Supports: clicking, transient swelling; Opposes: no locking/giving way, full ROM, no discrete twisting injury.
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; physiotherapy assessment first; imaging if indicated based on exam to evaluate cartilage/meniscus.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Activity modification: reduce running; avoid running through pain.
     - Ice therapy: continue regularly.
     - Medication: Prescribed a stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly with food; do not combine with ibuprofen/other NSAIDs. (Name/dose/route/frequency not documented.)
     - Safety-net: Return/seek urgent care for persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or true knee locking.
   - Relevant referrals: Physiotherapy referral placed; clinic visit if physiotherapy wait is excessive.
2. Transient right toe tingling post-run:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Peripheral nerve compression from footwear/lacing or peroneal nerve irritation – Low (DDx).
   - Differential diagnosis: None further prioritized given single transient episode and resolution; vascular etiologies not suggested by history.
   - Investigations planned: None at this time.
   - Treatment planned: Observation; no active intervention discussed.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation (exact doses, routes, frequencies) incomplete.
  - No vitals; no in-person knee examination or special tests.
  - No documentation of immunizations/COVID-19 vaccine status.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Initial statement referenced “knees hurting,” later clarified as right knee only (clarified during consult).
  - DDx labels Aleve as naproxen; patient was unsure of the drug class (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Clear overall with minor pauses; no objective exam possible via video; no numerical vitals reported.
